where: Windward Stair I & II (the switchback mountain route) + the Wind-Eye and Thunderroost spurs
mood: The Long Climb — airy, building, breath-quickening; each phrase re-launches a step higher so the loop feels like ascent.
core_styles: 16-bit console RPG soundtrack from the mid-1990s
retro sampled-chip instruments with the warm echo of a 16-bit sound chip
noble sampled French horn melody climbing in stepwise terraces
warm sampled string section carrying the harmony
plucked sampled bass stepping like footsteps on stone
sampled snare and timpani in a marching cadence, footsteps rather than a dance beat
soft wind swell cresting every four bars
mountain climbing route theme, determined, airy and adventurous, sunset thinning to cold blue

sections.name: Horn Call
sections.text: {a horn call rings out and echoes off the cliffs, the strings answer, and the march sets off on the next downbeat}

sections.name: Main Theme
sections.text: {the climbing melody on the horn: a rising leap that overshoots, then a stepwise settle, the phrase re-launched a step higher; snare and timpani march beneath}

sections.name: Main Theme Higher
sections.text: {the theme sequenced one step higher, strings doubling the horn, a bell counter-line glinting, the wind swell cresting at each switchback}

sections.name: Bridge
sections.text: {contrast: a breath on a ledge in F sharp minor and D major, a flute sings long notes over held strings looking out over the drop, then a timpani roll builds back up}

sections.name: Main Theme Return
sections.text: {the climb resumes at full stride, horns and strings together at their brightest; the last bar steps down to the E dominant and leads straight back into the theme}

_note: 2026-10: owner found the 132 BPM kick-and-snare version 'too dancey' — now a 116 BPM orchestral march on foot (horns, strings, snare + timpani, no kick).
